1. /**
2.  * Classes and extensions needed to read and parse rules configuration file
3.  */
4. 
5. package org.cqfn.diktat.common.config.rules
6. 
7. import org.cqfn.diktat.common.config.reader.JsonResourceConfigReader
8. import org.cqfn.diktat.common.config.rules.RulesConfigReader.Companion.log
9. 
10. import com.charleskorn.kaml.Yaml
11. import com.charleskorn.kaml.YamlConfiguration
12. import org.slf4j.Logger
13. import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory
14. 
15. import java.io.BufferedReader
16. import java.io.File
17. import java.util.Locale
18. import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger
19. 
20. import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable
21. import kotlinx.serialization.decodeFromString
22. 
23. /**
24.  * Name of common configuration
25.  */
26. const val DIKTAT_COMMON = "DIKTAT_COMMON"
27. 
28. /**
29.  * This interface represents individual inspection in rule set.
30.  */
31. interface Rule {
32.     /**
33.      * @return name of this [Rule]
34.      */
35.     fun ruleName(): String
36. }
37. 
38. /**
39.  * Configuration of individual [Rule]
40.  * @property name name of the rule
41.  * @property enabled
42.  * @property configuration a map of strings with configuration options
43.  */
44. @Serializable
45. data class RulesConfig(
46.     val name: String,
47.     val enabled: Boolean = true,
48.     val configuration: Map<String, String> = emptyMap()
49. )
50. 
51. /**
52.  * Configuration that allows customizing additional options of particular rules.
53.  * @property config a map of strings with configuration options for a particular rule
54.  */
55. open class RuleConfiguration(protected val config: Map<String, String>)
56. 
57. /**
58.  * class returns the list of configurations that we have read from a yml: diktat-analysis.yml
59.  * @property classLoader a [ClassLoader] used to load configuration file
60.  */
61. open class RulesConfigReader(override val classLoader: ClassLoader) : JsonResourceConfigReader<List<RulesConfig>>() {
62.     private val yamlSerializer by lazy { Yaml(configuration = YamlConfiguration(strictMode = true)) }
63. 
64.     /**
65.      * Parse resource file into list of [RulesConfig]
66.      *
67.      * @param fileStream a [BufferedReader] representing loaded rules config file
68.      * @return list of [RulesConfig]
69.      */
70.     override fun parseResource(fileStream: BufferedReader): List<RulesConfig> = fileStream.use { stream ->
71.         yamlSerializer.decodeFromString(stream.readLines().joinToString(separator = "\n"))
72.     }
73. 
74.     /**
75.      * instead of reading the resource as it is done in the interface we will read a file by the absolute path here
76.      * if the path is provided, else will read the hardcoded file 'diktat-analysis.yml' from the package
77.      *
78.      * @param resourceFileName name of the resource which will be loaded using [classLoader]
79.      * @return [BufferedReader] representing loaded resource
80.      */
81.     override fun getConfigFile(resourceFileName: String): BufferedReader? {
82.         val resourceFile = File(resourceFileName)
83.         return if (resourceFile.exists()) {
84.             log.debug("Using diktat-analysis.yml file from the following path: ${resourceFile.absolutePath}")
85.             File(resourceFileName).bufferedReader()
86.         } else {
87.             log.debug("Using the default diktat-analysis.yml file from the class path")
88.             classLoader.getResourceAsStream(resourceFileName)?.bufferedReader()
89.         }
90.     }
91. 
92.     companion object {
93.         /**
94.          * A [Logger] that can be used
95.          */
96.         val log: Logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger(RulesConfigReader::class.java)
97.     }
98. }
99. 
100. /**
101.  * class returns the list of common configurations that we have read from a configuration map
102.  *
103.  * @param configuration map of common configuration
104.  */
105. data class CommonConfiguration(private val configuration: Map<String, String>?) {
106.     /**
107.      * List of directory names which will be used to detect test sources
108.      */
109.     val testAnchors: List<String> by lazy {
110.         val testDirs = (configuration ?: emptyMap()).getOrDefault("testDirs", "test").split(',')
111.         if (testDirs.any { !it.lowercase(Locale.getDefault()).endsWith("test") }) {
112.             log.error("test directory names should end with `test`")
113.         }
114.         testDirs
115.     }
116. 
117.     /**
118.      * Start of package name, which shoould be common, e.g. org.example.myproject
119.      */
120.     val domainName: String? by lazy {
121.         configuration?.get("domainName")
122.     }
123. 
124.     /**
125.      * Get disable chapters from configuration
126.      */
127.     val disabledChapters: String? by lazy {
128.         configuration?.get("disabledChapters")
129.     }
130. 
131.     /**
132.      * Get version of kotlin from configuration
133.      */
134.     val kotlinVersion: KotlinVersion by lazy {
135.         configuration?.get("kotlinVersion")?.kotlinVersion() ?: run {
136.             if (visitorCounter.incrementAndGet() == 1) {
137.                 log.error("Kotlin version not specified in the configuration file. Will be using ${KotlinVersion.CURRENT} version")
138.             }
139.             KotlinVersion.CURRENT
140.         }
141.     }
142. 
143.     /**
144.      * Get source directories from configuration
145.      */
146.     val srcDirectories: List<String> by lazy {
147.         val srcDirs = configuration?.get("srcDirectories")?.split(",")?.map { it.trim() } ?: listOf("main")
148.         if (srcDirs.any { !it.lowercase(Locale.getDefault()).endsWith("main") }) {
149.             log.error("source directory names should end with `main`")
150.         }
151.         srcDirs
152.     }
153. 
154.     /**
155.      * False if configuration has been read from config file, true if defaults are used
156.      */
157.     val isDefault = configuration == null
158. 
159.     companion object {
160.         /**
161.          * Counter that helps not to raise multiple warnings about kotlin version
162.          */
163.         var visitorCounter = AtomicInteger(0)
164.     }
165. }
166. 
167. // ================== utils for List<RulesConfig> from yml config
168. 
169. /**
170.  * @return common configuration from list of all rules configuration
171.  */
172. fun List<RulesConfig>.getCommonConfiguration() = CommonConfiguration(getCommonConfig()?.configuration)
173. 
174. /**
175.  * Get [RulesConfig] for particular [Rule] object.
176.  *
177.  * @param rule a [Rule] which configuration will be returned
178.  * @return [RulesConfig] for a particular rule if it is found, else null
179.  */
180. fun List<RulesConfig>.getRuleConfig(rule: Rule): RulesConfig? = this.find { it.name == rule.ruleName() }
181. 
182. /**
183.  * checking if in yml config particular rule is enabled or disabled
184.  * (!) the default value is "true" (in case there is no config specified)
185.  *
186.  * @param rule a [Rule] which is being checked
187.  * @return true if rule is enabled in configuration, else false
188.  */
189. fun List<RulesConfig>.isRuleEnabled(rule: Rule): Boolean {
190.     val ruleMatched = getRuleConfig(rule)
191.     return ruleMatched?.enabled ?: true
192. }
193. 
194. /**
195.  * Parse string into KotlinVersion
196.  *
197.  * @return KotlinVersion from configuration
198.  */
199. fun String.kotlinVersion(): KotlinVersion {
200.     require(this.contains("^(\\d+\\.)(\\d+)\\.?(\\d+)?$".toRegex())) {
201.         "Kotlin version format is incorrect"
202.     }
203.     val versions = this.split(".").map { it.toInt() }
204.     return if (versions.size == 2) {
205.         KotlinVersion(versions[0], versions[1])
206.     } else {
207.         KotlinVersion(versions[0], versions[1], versions[2])
208.     }
209. }
210. 
211. /**
212.  * Get [RulesConfig] representing common configuration part that can be used in any rule
213.  */
214. private fun List<RulesConfig>.getCommonConfig() = find { it.name == DIKTAT_COMMON }
215.

64. /**
65.  * Rule that checks indentation. The following general rules are checked:
66.  * 1. Only spaces should be used each indentation is equal to 4 spaces
67.  * 2. File should end with new line
68.  * Additionally, a set of CustomIndentationChecker objects checks all WHITE_SPACE node if they are exceptions from general rules.
69.  * @see CustomIndentationChecker
70.  */
71. @Suppress("LargeClass")
72. class IndentationRule(configRules: List<RulesConfig>) : DiktatRule(
73.     "indentation",
74.     configRules,
75.     listOf(WRONG_INDENTATION)) {
76.     private val configuration: IndentationConfig by lazy {
77.         IndentationConfig(configRules.getRuleConfig(WRONG_INDENTATION)?.configuration ?: emptyMap())
78.     }
79.     private lateinit var filePath: String
80.     private lateinit var customIndentationCheckers: List<CustomIndentationChecker>
81. 
82.     override fun logic(node: ASTNode) {
83.         if (node.elementType == FILE) {
84.             filePath = node.getFilePath()
85. 
86.             customIndentationCheckers = listOf(
87.                 ::AssignmentOperatorChecker,
88.                 ::ConditionalsAndLoopsWithoutBracesChecker,
89.                 ::SuperTypeListChecker,
90.                 ::ValueParameterListChecker,
91.                 ::ExpressionIndentationChecker,
92.                 ::DotCallChecker,
93.                 ::KdocIndentationChecker,
94.                 ::CustomGettersAndSettersChecker,
95.                 ::ArrowInWhenChecker
96.             ).map { it.invoke(configuration) }
97. 
98.             if (checkIsIndentedWithSpaces(node)) {
99.                 checkIndentation(node)
100.             } else {
101.                 log.warn("Not going to check indentation because there are tabs")
102.             }
103.             checkNewlineAtEnd(node)
104.         }
105.     }
106. 
107.     /**
108.      * This method warns if tabs are used in WHITE_SPACE nodes and substitutes them with spaces in fix mode
109.      *
110.      * @return true if there are no tabs or all of them have been fixed, false otherwise
111.      */
112.     @Suppress("FUNCTION_BOOLEAN_PREFIX")
113.     private fun checkIsIndentedWithSpaces(node: ASTNode): Boolean {
114.         val whiteSpaceNodes: MutableList<ASTNode> = mutableListOf()
115.         node.getAllLeafsWithSpecificType(WHITE_SPACE, whiteSpaceNodes)
116.         whiteSpaceNodes
117.             .filter { it.textContains('\t') }
118.             .apply {
119.                 if (isEmpty()) {
120.                     return true
121.                 }
122.             }
123.             .forEach {
124.                 WRONG_INDENTATION.warnAndFix(configRules, emitWarn, isFixMode, "tabs are not allowed for indentation", it.startOffset + it.text.indexOf('\t'), it) {
125.                     (it as LeafPsiElement).rawReplaceWithText(it.text.replace("\t", " ".repeat(configuration.indentationSize)))
126.                 }
127.             }
128.         return isFixMode  // true if we changed all tabs to spaces
129.     }
130. 
131.     /**
132.      * Checks that file ends with exactly one empty line
133.      */
134.     private fun checkNewlineAtEnd(node: ASTNode) {
135.         if (configuration.newlineAtEnd) {
136.             val lastChild = generateSequence(node) { it.lastChildNode }.last()
137.             val numBlankLinesAfter = lastChild.text.count { it == '\n' }
138.             if (lastChild.elementType != WHITE_SPACE || numBlankLinesAfter != 1) {
139.                 val warnText = if (lastChild.elementType != WHITE_SPACE || numBlankLinesAfter == 0) "no newline" else "too many blank lines"
140.                 val fileName = filePath.substringAfterLast(File.separator)
141.                 // In case, when last child is newline, visually user will see blank line at the end of file,
142.                 // however, the text length does not consider it, since it's blank and line appeared only because of `\n`
143.                 // But ktlint synthetically increase length in aim to have ability to point to this line, so in this case
144.                 // offset will be `node.textLength`, otherwise we will point to the last symbol, i.e `node.textLength - 1`
145.                 val offset = if (lastChild.elementType == WHITE_SPACE && lastChild.textContains('\n')) node.textLength else node.textLength - 1
146.                 WRONG_INDENTATION.warnAndFix(configRules, emitWarn, isFixMode, "$warnText at the end of file $fileName", offset, node) {
147.                     if (lastChild.elementType != WHITE_SPACE) {
148.                         node.addChild(PsiWhiteSpaceImpl("\n"), null)
149.                     } else {
150.                         lastChild.leaveOnlyOneNewLine()
151.                     }
152.                 }
153.             }
154.         }
155.     }

157.     /**
158.      * Traverses the tree, keeping track of regular and exceptional indentations
159.      */
160.     private fun checkIndentation(node: ASTNode) {
161.         val context = IndentContext(configuration)
162.         node.visit { astNode ->
163.             context.checkAndReset(astNode)
164.             if (astNode.elementType in increasingTokens) {
165.                 context.storeIncrementingToken(astNode.elementType)
166.             } else if (astNode.elementType in decreasingTokens && !astNode.treePrev.let { it.elementType == WHITE_SPACE && it.textContains('\n') }) {
167.                 // if decreasing token is after WHITE_SPACE with \n, indents are corrected in visitWhiteSpace method
168.                 context.dec(astNode.elementType)
169.             } else if (astNode.elementType == WHITE_SPACE && astNode.textContains('\n') && astNode.treeNext != null) {
170.                 // we check only WHITE_SPACE nodes with newlines, other than the last line in file; correctness of newlines should be checked elsewhere
171.                 visitWhiteSpace(astNode, context)
172.             }
173.         }
174.     }
175. 
176.     @Suppress("ForbiddenComment")
177.     private fun visitWhiteSpace(astNode: ASTNode, context: IndentContext) {
178.         context.maybeIncrement()
179. 
180.         val whiteSpace = astNode.psi as PsiWhiteSpace
181.         if (astNode.treeNext.elementType in decreasingTokens) {
182.             // if newline is followed by closing token, it should already be indented less
183.             context.dec(astNode.treeNext.elementType)
184.         }
185. 
186.         val indentError = IndentationError(context.indent(), astNode.text.lastIndent())
187. 
188.         val checkResult = customIndentationCheckers.firstNotNullResult {
189.             it.checkNode(whiteSpace, indentError)
190.         }
191. 
192.         val expectedIndent = checkResult?.expectedIndent ?: indentError.expected
193.         if (checkResult?.adjustNext == true && astNode.parents().none { it.elementType == LONG_STRING_TEMPLATE_ENTRY }) {
194.             val exceptionInitiatorNode = astNode.getExceptionalIndentInitiator()
195.             context.addException(exceptionInitiatorNode, expectedIndent - indentError.expected, checkResult.includeLastChild)
196.         }
197. 
198.         if (astNode.treeParent.elementType == LONG_STRING_TEMPLATE_ENTRY && indentError.expected != indentError.actual) {
199.             context.addException(astNode.treeParent, abs(indentError.expected - indentError.actual), false)
200.         }
201. 
202.         if (checkResult?.isCorrect != true && expectedIndent != indentError.actual) {
203.             WRONG_INDENTATION.warnAndFix(configRules, emitWarn, isFixMode, "expected $expectedIndent but was ${indentError.actual}",
204.                 whiteSpace.startOffset + whiteSpace.text.lastIndexOf('\n') + 1, whiteSpace.node) {
205.                 checkStringLiteral(whiteSpace, expectedIndent, indentError.actual)
206.                 whiteSpace.node.indentBy(expectedIndent)
207.             }
208.         }
209.     }

211.     /**
212.      * Checks if it is triple-quoted string template with trimIndent() or trimMargin() function.
213.      */
214.     private fun checkStringLiteral(
215.         whiteSpace: PsiWhiteSpace,
216.         expectedIndent: Int,
217.         actualIndent: Int
218.     ) {
219.         val nextNode = whiteSpace.node.treeNext
220.         if (nextNode != null &&
221.                 nextNode.elementType == DOT_QUALIFIED_EXPRESSION &&
222.                 nextNode.firstChildNode.elementType == STRING_TEMPLATE &&
223.                 nextNode.firstChildNode.text.startsWith("\"\"\"") &&
224.                 nextNode.findChildByType(CALL_EXPRESSION)?.text?.let {
225.                     it == "trimIndent()" ||
226.                             it == "trimMargin()"
227.                 } == true) {
228.             fixStringLiteral(whiteSpace, expectedIndent, actualIndent)
229.         }
230.     }
231. 
232.     /**
233.      * If it is triple-quoted string template we need to indent all its parts
234.      */
235.     private fun fixStringLiteral(
236.         whiteSpace: PsiWhiteSpace,
237.         expectedIndent: Int,
238.         actualIndent: Int
239.     ) {
240.         val textIndent = " ".repeat(expectedIndent + INDENT_SIZE)
241.         val templateEntries = whiteSpace.node.treeNext.firstChildNode.getAllChildrenWithType(LITERAL_STRING_TEMPLATE_ENTRY)
242.         templateEntries.forEach { node ->
243.             if (!node.text.contains("\n")) {
244.                 fixFirstTemplateEntries(node, textIndent, actualIndent)
245.             }
246.         }
247.         (templateEntries.last().firstChildNode as LeafPsiElement)
248.             .rawReplaceWithText(" ".repeat(expectedIndent) + templateEntries
249.                 .last()
250.                 .firstChildNode
251.                 .text
252.                 .trim())
253.     }
254. 
255.     /**
256.      * This method fixes all lines of string template except the last one
257.      * Also it considers $foo insertions in string
258.      */
259.     private fun fixFirstTemplateEntries(
260.         node: ASTNode,
261.         textIndent: String,
262.         actualIndent: Int
263.     ) {
264.         val correctedText = StringBuilder()
265.         // shift of the node depending on its initial string template indent
266.         val nodeStartIndent = if (node.firstChildNode.text.takeWhile { it == ' ' }.count() - actualIndent - INDENT_SIZE > 0) {
267.             node.firstChildNode.text.takeWhile { it == ' ' }.count() - actualIndent - INDENT_SIZE
268.         } else {
269.             0
270.         }
271.         val isPrevStringTemplate = node.treePrev.elementType in stringLiteralTokens
272.         val isNextStringTemplate = node.treeNext.elementType in stringLiteralTokens
273.         when {
274.             // if string template is before literal_string
275.             isPrevStringTemplate && !isNextStringTemplate -> correctedText.append(node.firstChildNode.text.trimEnd())
276.             // if string template is after literal_string
277.             !isPrevStringTemplate && isNextStringTemplate -> correctedText.append(textIndent + " ".repeat(nodeStartIndent) + node.firstChildNode.text.trimStart())
278.             // if there is no string template in literal_string
279.             !isPrevStringTemplate && !isNextStringTemplate -> correctedText.append(textIndent + " ".repeat(nodeStartIndent) + node.firstChildNode.text.trim())
280.             isPrevStringTemplate && isNextStringTemplate -> correctedText.append(node.firstChildNode.text)
281.             node.text.isBlank() -> correctedText.append(textIndent)
282.             else -> {}
283.         }
284.         (node.firstChildNode as LeafPsiElement).rawReplaceWithText(correctedText.toString())
285.     }
286. 
287.     private fun ASTNode.getExceptionalIndentInitiator() = treeParent.let { parent ->
288.         when (parent.psi) {
289.             // fixme: custom logic for determining exceptional indent initiator, should be moved elsewhere
290.             // get the topmost expression to keep extended indent for the whole chain of dot call expressions
291.             is KtDotQualifiedExpression -> parents().takeWhile { it.elementType == DOT_QUALIFIED_EXPRESSION || it.elementType == SAFE_ACCESS_EXPRESSION }.last()
292.             is KtIfExpression -> parent.findChildByType(THEN) ?: parent.findChildByType(ELSE) ?: parent
293.             is KtLoopExpression -> (parent.psi as KtLoopExpression).body?.node ?: parent
294.             else -> parent
295.         }
296.     }
297. 
298.     /**
299.      * Class that contains state needed to calculate indent and keep track of exceptional indents.
300.      * Tokens from [increasingTokens] are stored in stack [activeTokens]. When [WHITE_SPACE] with line break is encountered,
301.      * if stack is not empty, indentation is increased. When token from [decreasingTokens] is encountered, it's counterpart is removed
302.      * from stack. If there has been a [WHITE_SPACE] with line break between them, indentation is decreased.
303.      */
304.     private class IndentContext(private val config: IndentationConfig) {
305.         private var regularIndent = 0
306.         private val exceptionalIndents: MutableList<ExceptionalIndent> = mutableListOf()
307.         private val activeTokens: Stack<IElementType> = Stack()
308. 
309.         /**
310.          * @param token a token that caused indentation increment, for example an opening brace
311.          * @return Unit
312.          */
313.         fun storeIncrementingToken(token: IElementType) = token
314.             .also { require(it in increasingTokens) { "Only tokens that increase indentation should be passed to this method" } }
315.             .let(activeTokens::push)
316. 
317.         /**
318.          * Checks whether indentation needs to be incremented and increments in this case.
319.          */
320.         fun maybeIncrement() {
321.             if (activeTokens.isNotEmpty() && activeTokens.peek() != WHITE_SPACE) {
322.                 regularIndent += config.indentationSize
323.                 activeTokens.push(WHITE_SPACE)
324.             }
325.         }
326. 
327.         /**
328.          * @param token a token that caused indentation decrement, for example a closing brace
329.          */
330.         fun dec(token: IElementType) {
331.             if (activeTokens.peek() == WHITE_SPACE) {
332.                 while (activeTokens.peek() == WHITE_SPACE) {
333.                     activeTokens.pop()
334.                 }
335.                 regularIndent -= config.indentationSize
336.             }
337.             if (activeTokens.isNotEmpty() && activeTokens.peek() == matchingTokens.find { it.second == token }?.first) {
338.                 activeTokens.pop()
339.             }
340.         }
341. 
342.         /**
343.          * @return full current indent
344.          */
345.         fun indent() = regularIndent + exceptionalIndents.sumOf { it.indent }
346. 
347.         /**
348.          * @param initiator a node that caused exceptional indentation
349.          * @param indent an additional indent
350.          * @param includeLastChild whether the last child node should be included in the range affected by exceptional indentation
351.          * @return true if add exception in exceptionalIndents
352.          */
353.         fun addException(
354.             initiator: ASTNode,
355.             indent: Int,
356.             includeLastChild: Boolean) =
357.                 exceptionalIndents.add(ExceptionalIndent(initiator, indent, includeLastChild))
358. 
359.         /**
360.          * @param astNode the node which is used to determine whether exceptinoal indents are still active
361.          * @return boolean result
362.          */
363.         fun checkAndReset(astNode: ASTNode) = exceptionalIndents.retainAll { it.isActive(astNode) }
364. 
365.         /**
366.          * @property initiator a node that caused exceptional indentation
367.          * @property indent an additional indent
368.          * @property includeLastChild whether the last child node should be included in the range affected by exceptional indentation
369.          */
370.         private data class ExceptionalIndent(
371.             val initiator: ASTNode,
372.             val indent: Int,
373.             val includeLastChild: Boolean = true) {
374.             /**
375.              * Checks whether this exceptional indent is still active. This is a hypotheses that exceptional indentation will end
376.              * outside of node where it appeared, e.g. when an expression after assignment operator is over.
377.              *
378.              * @param currentNode the current node during AST traversal
379.              * @return boolean result
380.              */
381.             fun isActive(currentNode: ASTNode): Boolean = currentNode.psi.parentsWithSelf.any { it.node == initiator } &&
382.                     (includeLastChild || currentNode.treeNext != initiator.lastChildNode)
383.         }
384.     }
385. 
386.     companion object {
387.         private val log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(IndentationRule::class.java)
388.         const val INDENT_SIZE = 4
389.         private val increasingTokens = listOf(LPAR, LBRACE, LBRACKET, LONG_TEMPLATE_ENTRY_START)
390.         private val decreasingTokens = listOf(RPAR, RBRACE, RBRACKET, LONG_TEMPLATE_ENTRY_END)
391.         private val matchingTokens = increasingTokens.zip(decreasingTokens)
392.         private val stringLiteralTokens = listOf(SHORT_STRING_TEMPLATE_ENTRY, LONG_STRING_TEMPLATE_ENTRY)
393.     }
394. }
395. 
396. /**
397.  * @property expected expected indentation as a number of spaces
398.  * @property actual actual indentation as a number of spaces
399.  */
400. internal data class IndentationError(val expected: Int, val actual: Int)
401. 
402. /**
403.  * @return indentation of the last line of this string
404.  */
405. internal fun String.lastIndent() = substringAfterLast('\n').count { it == ' ' }
